history.value: Accel was founded in Palo Alto in 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz, around the idea that chance favors the prepared mind. It opened in London in 2000 and India in 2008, and was an early backer of Facebook, Slack, Atlassian, CrowdStrike, Spotify and Flipkart. It runs one global partnership and raised new London and India funds in 2026.

investment_range.basis: Median: partner-anchored entry-round median $19,597,993 across 155 membership-verified base companies with priced Form D histories (473 rounds; 55 entries anchored past pre-investor rounds, 1 weak anchor), on the Common Crawl-rebuilt base (886 members), the expanded 217-person-roster sweep (1,086 accessions) and the refreshed issuer-rounds rescan (7a7fc8f), published as $20M. p10 $4.7M, p25 $9.4M, p75 $43.5M, p90 $100.0M. Pre-base corroboration: $22.0M over the 63 site-list-confirmed issuers of the roster sweep. A round-size proxy for check size, fair for a high-ownership lead investor. | Lower limit: Accel Atoms pre-seed program, 'up to $1 million' per company (atoms.accel.com, Atoms 4.0; up to $2M co-investment in the 2026 AI cohort); the program states a cap, not a floor. | Upper limit: the $2.3B Cursor (Anysphere) Series D co-led by Accel and Coatue at $29.3B, November 2025 (CNBC 2025-11-13); a led-round figure, not a single-check claim. Dry-powder check: Leaders V ($4B) at 10-15% single-position concentration supports $400-600M positions, and TechCrunch reports ~$200M average checks from that fund

funds.basis: 27 funds, vintage 2015-2026, from the full 'Accel *' Form D filer sweep on EDGAR company search (59 own filing vehicles, 62 Form D filings) cross-checked against the base session's partner-anchored sweep. Direct raises carry filed sold amounts asserted against the filings at build time (20 entries with accessions); where the L.P. filed sold $0 (Growth V/8, 17, London 9, India IV/VII/9, Leaders 5) the press size is published and the filing's total offering amount corroborates it exactly in every case. Excluded from the list, to avoid double-counting and sub-scale vehicles: Strategic Partners / Entrepreneurs partner-money parallels ($7.6M-$95M sold), the internal Accel Investors co-invest LLC/LP series (ADV roster), Leaders 4/5 Opportunities (C) sidecars ($59M sold / $25M offered), and Accel Circle Fund 2026 L.P. ($95M offering, no public size; classified as the internal co-invest class, decisions.md #6). Accel Core L.P. is included as the Leaders V LP sidecar at its filed $749.6M close. Pre-2015 families (XI/XII, Growth II/III, London IV, India III and earlier) predate the 10-year window. Accel-KKR vehicles are a separate firm (decisions.md #2) and are excluded from the sweep entirely

flags.note: Scope: the 35 people the firm's own team page publishes, investors only; no operations staff is published (out of ~300 employees, Wikipedia 2024). The site shows no role labels on cards; 28 of 35 profile metaDescriptions state 'Partner' and the remaining 7 (all partners by press record) render the site's flat 'Partner' presentation via the build fallback. One member (Kevin Comolli) is filed under the site's Emeritus bucket but published on the team page and is kept. Socials from the site CMS: 30 LinkedIn, 23 X.

Where press and filing disagree the filed amount is published: India V $430M (press $450M), India VI $525M (press $550M), Leaders 3 $2.255B (press $2.3-2.35B), Growth IV $1.2B (press bundled $1.5B incl. the $300M Leaders Fund). Leaders 5 vintage is 2026 (announced April 2026) though its first Form D is 2025q4; India VIII vintage 2024 (filed 2024q4) though announced January 2025. Growth Fund 8 is the vehicle press calls the $1.35B 'global expansion fund'.

The issue expected bottom = US RAUM, top = press ~$36B; at run time the sworn numbers came in above press (RAUM $38.03B alone), so both ends are sworn instead: bottom US-umbrella RAUM, top RAUM + London ERAs' 7.B gross assets ($8.80B, deduplicated identical rosters). The April 2026 press ~$36B predates the August 2026 $3.5B raise and RAUM counts uncalled commitments. 2026-vintage vehicles (17, Growth 8, London 9, India 9, Circle, Core) postdate the FY2025 ADV and are in neither figure.

Median recomputed on the membership-complete base and again on the Common Crawl rebuild (both 2026-08-31): $19.6M over 155 verified members, vs $22.0M on the pre-base site-confirmed subset. Priced Form D rounds only; SAFE and 4(a)(2) seeds don't file, so the small end is under-sampled, and a few tails may ride weak CIK joins (the base run's standing weak-CIK audit is the cleanup; the median is insensitive to them). The partner-anchored first filing is a ceiling on entry recency, so some anchors sit later than the true entry round (e.g. UiPath anchors at a $230M round though Accel led the 2017 Series A). Floor: Atoms states 'up to $1M', a cap, not a floor. Ceiling is the co-led round figure (Cursor $2.3B), Accel's own share undisclosed. Stable across three populations (63 pre-base, 131 rebuild, 155 refreshed rescan): $22.0M / $20.0M / $19.6M. Rebuilds again only if IA recovers before sign-off.

The firm's own vocabulary is seed / series-a entry types plus Early/Late Stage filters, a Growth fund family and a Leaders late-stage family; Pre-Seed rests on the Atoms program ruling (decisions.md #4). Series B is deliberately not claimed: the firm's own language never names it, unlike a16z's 'Venture' split. Trim in review if too wide.

Core carries three labels (US, Europe, India) per PRO-68's explicit instruction, exceeding PRO-7's cap of two for the leaderboard row (core joins with commas in a narrow column). Erik's call at review: keep three or demote India to other. 'Oceania' in other is the site's own region label (4 rows incl. Atlassian) and is outside geo.json's known values; geo is open vocabulary so it passes with a warning.

All eight verified as ledger member verdicts on the membership-complete base; the build gate keys on ledger verdicts, not status auto_confirmed, because wayback-pending single-source rows (Flipkart, Spotify, Supercell) legitimately sit needs_review while being members. Spotify and Supercell selected over UiPath/Qualtrics on household recognition; swap in review if preferred.

Focus derives from the site's own 48-tag sector vocabulary (count-weighted crosswalk, 9 values above the 25-company threshold); Climate & Energy and Crypto & Web3 stay out (site tags Crypto 13, Web3 8, Climate ~5, below threshold). The crosswalk is staged for config.json profile.focus_crosswalk (base session owns the file); the base-tag recompute publishes automatically when base tag coverage reaches 25%.
